replies.author: mmmm
replies.text:
You could introduce it as an entirely new, but android compatible OS. I mean - that's what it is really. Frame it like this: iOS for iPhone, android for other phones, GrapheneOS for pixels (and soon Motorola). You could suggest that with ios you end up locked in. You could suggest android is spyware, as in anything you do on an android phone is essentially visible to the manufacturer of the phone and Google. You could frame grapheneOS as a solution to those two problems. There is no lock in and there is no surveillance built in. You could explain it in a way that suggests the phone becomes what you want it to be instead of what the company who sold the phone wants it to be.

One thing that I have done to make other people more aware (read: scared) is to talk about the keyboard. Anything that is typed potentially can be read. Not so with GrapheneOS and the right selection of keyboard and the correct settings.

People are often not worried about abstract (to them) ideas. But if people understand that anything they type has potential to be seen then they think in different terms.
